title: Quadlet .build manual
body:
### Feature request description

Hello there,

Currently, the only way to run `.build` files is to reference them in a `.container` or go through some `podman-system-generator` shenanigans.


The Rationale for this is to allow for consistent way of defining image build details for development vs production. 

Right now we deploy our quadlets with `.image` in production and in dev use overrides to point to a `.build` file. However, in our CI there is no readily way of build the images from `.build` files so we have to keep the `.build` file and `podman build` commands manually in sync.

As a side, `podman quadlet run` is also something to consider, as way to run to allow running a `.container` file. This is somewhat tangentially related to  #29804 as well.

comments.body:
If you want to run a build file you can just `systemctl start <name>-build.service` to start the build service for the quadlet file after you did `systemctl daemon-reload` to trigger the quadlet generator.

Running these files directly makes no sense because all settings are amied towards the systemd integration and we recommend people using things like systemd specifiers and using other non podman options ExecStartPre= and unit dependencies with Wants/Before/After,etc...

So overall I would this makes no sense to support directly with a podman command.
cc @ygalblum
I agree with @Luap99 . We need to keep in mind what Quadlet is. It is a systemd generator for Podman. So, "invoking" it should be done using systemd commands (as stated above)

In my estimate, running `systemctl start <name>-build.service` in CI is a bit awkward. Right now there is no way to document/spec building of images for quadlets in CI without attempting to run the services. Those are two different concerns.

I should be able to build images on demand, in way that matches exactly what the `systemctl start <name>-build.service` would do.

Qualdet is not a generic declarative way to run podman commands. It is a systemd-generator. Moreover, as @Luap99 mentioned, it supports passing Systemd specific specifiers and non-podman options. As such, it creates systemd units that can be managed via systemctl commands. 
Therefore, I think that a `podman quadlet run` does not make sense

I think it is not necessary that quadlet bypass systemd for these task for that distinction to matter. It is only helpful for it to proovide the ergonomics of using quadlet with a CI easier. This wouldn't be an entirely new concept anyways, since `quadlet install` already supports `--reload-systemd ` for example.
